items.stem: Which type of entity is generally NOT eligible to apply the IFRS for SMEs standard?

options.text: An entity with public accountability, such as one whose shares are publicly traded
options.rationale: Correct: publicly accountable entities are not eligible.

options.text: A small private company with no public accountability
options.rationale: Such an entity is typically eligible.

options.text: A family-owned manufacturer that does not file with a securities regulator
options.rationale: This is the kind of entity the SME standard is designed for.

options.text: A private start-up with few owners
options.rationale: A private start-up without public accountability can qualify.

items.explanation: Correct: publicly accountable entities are not eligible.

items.stem: Which TWO treatments differ in the IFRS for SMEs standard compared with full IFRS? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Goodwill is amortised over its useful life rather than only tested for impairment
options.rationale: Correct: the SME standard amortises goodwill, unlike full IFRS.

options.text: Development costs are expensed rather than capitalised when criteria are met
options.rationale: Correct: the SME standard expenses development (and borrowing) costs, simplifying full IFRS.

options.text: SMEs must apply every disclosure required by full IFRS
options.rationale: The SME standard reduces disclosures, it does not require all of them.

options.text: SMEs must revalue all property, plant and equipment every year
options.rationale: No such annual revaluation requirement applies.

items.explanation: Correct: the SME standard amortises goodwill, unlike full IFRS.

items.stem: A company argues that because it is small, it automatically qualifies for the IFRS for SMEs standard. Why may this reasoning be wrong?

options.text: Eligibility depends on the absence of public accountability, not merely on size
options.rationale: Correct: a small but publicly accountable entity is not eligible.

options.text: Only very large entities can use the SME standard
options.rationale: That is the opposite of its purpose.

options.text: Size is the only criterion that matters
options.rationale: Public accountability, not size alone, governs eligibility.

options.text: The SME standard is mandatory for all companies
options.rationale: It is not mandatory for all companies.

items.explanation: Correct: a small but publicly accountable entity is not eligible.
